entries.description: Target selected: the EML Weierstrass theorem (T2.C open target, general case). BOUNDARY: the AI enumerated the five open targets and recommended this one; the human ratified. Is that direction-by-human or direction-by-AI? Logged as direction with the ? flag rather than resolved in favour of either, because resolving it silently would be the exact bias E2 exists to measure.
Caught own error: inserted a docstring between an existing docstring and its theorem, twice, breaking the parse both times. Second occurrence after the first was already fixed.

Chose to machine-check non-vacuity rather than assert it. No error existed — the theorem was already proved and would have passed every gate. hsmall and hmult constrain the same r from opposite directions, so a vacuous statement was a live possibility the gates are structurally blind to.

Noticed that the four intervention kinds record what happened but never who, so AI self-catches would confirm the human-outer-loop hypothesis for the wrong reason. Amendment 1 written. Logged actor=ai because this catch was also mine — which is precisely the pattern the amendment exists to make visible.

Refined the claim under test: not 'who catches errors' but 'where does the chain terminate'. Directed that catch-class entries record whether the catch fired inside a human-installed structure or arose unprompted, on the grounds that it is cheap now and unrecoverable retroactively.

Judged that the AI's visibility warning (all interventions logged as ai/unrecorded) was a finding about the claim rather than a caveat about the ledger. No error existed; the warning was correct as written. The judgement was that it changed what the experiment measures.

findings.description: T2.C term bound lifted from the two classical constants to the whole lacunary family in Lean; zero new axioms, identical axiom set to the specific case. Closes the 'not Lean-formalised' flag on the half of the EML Weierstrass theorem that was already proved on paper.
field_simp, linarith, by_contra unavailable in MachLib (Mathlib-free); div_lt_of_lt_mul exists only in a distant module. Working idiom is rcases lt_total + mach_ring + local re-derivation.

T2.C restriction (i) discharged: general-kernel term bound proved for the geometric-decay class, with a machine-checked non-vacuity witness. The heat-kernel results become one instance rather than the mechanism.
